CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Anderson is a 44-year-old female presenting with left shoulder pain that has been ongoing for one week. The pain began during a gymnastics class when the patient believes she may have fallen or assumed an awkward position during a particular move. The patient attempted self-treatment with Tylenol for 2-3 days without relief. She reports that any movement of the left shoulder causes pain, including forward and backward motion. She denies taking any pain medications prior to the visit other than the Tylenol trial.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports left shoulder pain with movement. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Prior surgery on left arm.

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol (trial for 2-3 days, ineffective).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient participates in gymnastics classes.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Physical examination reveals left shoulder tenderness with limited range of motion. Pain is elicited with forward and backward shoulder movement. X-ray of the left shoulder does not show evidence of fracture or broken bone.

RESULTS
X-ray of left shoulder: No fracture or broken bone identified.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left shoulder joint injury, likely strain or mild sprain from gymnastics activity. Patient advised to rest left arm for 3-4 weeks and avoid heavy lifting. Prescribed ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily for one week. Alternative pain management with ice or heat pad as needed. Patient may also use Advil or Aleve as alternatives. Follow-up appointment in 3 weeks to reassess. If pain persists after 3 weeks, consider repeat imaging. Patient instructed to contact office if symptoms worsen or do not improve prior to scheduled follow-up.
